message.content:
**LangChain** is an open‑source framework designed to help developers build applications that combine large language models (LLMs) with external data sources, tools, and workflows. It abstracts away many of the repetitive tasks involved in creating “chain”‑based logic—hence the name—so you can focus on the higher‑level design of your AI‑powered system.

Key points:

| Feature | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Chain building** | Lets you link together prompts, LLM calls, and other operations (e.g., API calls, database queries) in a declarative way. |
| **Tool integration** | Provides adapters for common services (SQL databases, APIs, web scraping, etc.) so the LLM can “call” them as part of its reasoning. |
| **Memory & context** | Offers built‑in mechanisms to store conversation history or other stateful information across turns. |
| **Prompt management** | Supports reusable prompt templates, dynamic prompt generation, and prompt injection protection. |
| **Agent support** | Includes pre‑built agent patterns (e.g., “retrieval‑augmented generation”, “tool‑using agents”) that can decide which tool to use next. |
| **Extensibility** | You can plug in any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, local models, etc.) and extend the framework with custom components. |

Typical use cases include:

- Building chatbots that can browse the web or query a database on demand.
- Creating data‑driven assistants that pull in real‑time metrics or reports.
- Automating workflows where an LLM decides which API calls to make next.
- Rapid prototyping of generative AI applications without writing boilerplate code.

In short, LangChain gives you a higher‑level, modular way to orchestrate LLMs with external tools, making it easier to build sophisticated, context‑aware AI applications.
